title: Number Quest Unit 4 · The Map Room (Pro)

items.q: Each list gives pairs (hours, kilometers) for one walker. In which list is the distance proportional to the time?
misconceptions: chose a list that adds the same amount each hour after a head start
correct
chose a list where the distance is the hours squared
added 4 to the hours instead of multiplying them
items.why: Divide each distance by its time. In (1, 4), (2, 8), (3, 12) every answer is 4, so d = 4t. In the other lists the answers change, for example 4 ÷ 1 = 4 but 6 ÷ 2 = 3.

items.q: A pump fills a tank at a steady rate: 10 liters after 4 minutes, 20 liters after 8 minutes, 30 liters after 12 minutes. What is the constant of proportionality, in liters per minute?
misconceptions: divided the minutes by the liters
subtracted 4 from 10 instead of dividing
correct
took the first amount as the rate
items.why: Liters per minute means liters divided by minutes: 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5. The other rows agree: 20 ÷ 8 = 2.5 and 30 ÷ 12 = 2.5.

items.q: The graph of distance against time for a walk is a straight line. Which extra fact makes the relationship proportional?
choices: The line goes up from left to right
misconceptions: thought any rising line is proportional
confused the point for 1 with the origin
linked steepness to being proportional
correct
items.why: A proportional graph is a straight line through the origin: at 0 hours the distance is 0. A straight line that starts higher, such as d = 2t + 1, is not proportional.

items.q: A map has a scale of 1 cm : 200 m. Two wells are 8 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they on the ground?
misconceptions: added the map distance to the scale
divided the scale by the map distance
dropped a zero when multiplying
correct
items.why: Every centimeter stands for 200 meters, so 8 centimeters stand for 8 × 200 = 1600 meters. Check by dividing: 1600 ÷ 200 = 8.

items.q: On a map, 1 cm stands for 50 m. With c for centimeters on the map and d for meters on the ground, which equation is right?
misconceptions: correct
swapped the map distance and the ground distance
added the scale instead of multiplying by it
treated the scale as a total of the two distances
items.why: Each centimeter is 50 meters, so the meters are 50 times the centimeters: d = 50c. Check with c = 2: d = 100, and 2 cm on the map is 100 m.

items.q: A room on a plan is 4 cm by 3 cm. The scale is 1 cm : 2 m. What is the real area of the room?
misconceptions: multiplied the paper area by the scale only once
correct
used the paper lengths without the scale
added the two real sides instead of multiplying
items.why: Scale each side first: 4 cm is 8 m and 3 cm is 6 m. The real area is 8 × 6 = 48 square meters. Each square centimeter stands for 2 × 2 = 4 square meters.

items.q: A plant was 20 cm tall. Now it is 25 cm tall. What is the percent increase?
misconceptions: divided the change by the new height
took the centimeters of change as the percent
gave the new height as a percent of the old height
correct
items.why: The change is 25 − 20 = 5 cm. Compare it with the start: 5 ÷ 20 = 0.25, which is 25%. Check: 25% of 20 is 5, and 20 + 5 = 25.

items.q: A scale shows 76 grams for a weight that is really 80 grams. What is the percent error?
misconceptions: took the grams of error as the percent
gave the reading as a percent of the real weight
correct
divided the error by the reading instead of the real weight
items.why: The reading is 80 − 76 = 4 grams off. Percent error compares that with the real value: 4 ÷ 80 = 0.05, which is 5%.

items.q: A tent is marked at $60. Ms. Okoro has a 25% discount. How much does she pay for the tent?
misconceptions: found the discount and stopped there
correct
subtracted 25 dollars instead of 25%
added the discount instead of subtracting it
items.why: 25% of 60 is 15, so the discount is $15. She pays 60 − 15 = $45. Another way: she pays 75% of 60, and 0.75 × 60 = 45.
